resolved_findings.finding: Each dispatch checks the single absolute stage deadline; generate also installs SIGALRM, SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers. BatchInterrupted inherits BaseException, so the original FunctionsRuntime Exception handler cannot swallow it into an ordinary tool error and continue. The enclosing BaseException path cancels the timer, stops the loop and preserves failure artifacts. Final cleanup restores handlers. Execution does not proceed into another case after interruption.
resolved_findings.limits: The deadline governs simulator execution, not guaranteed end-to-end cleanup latency. Bounded artifact finalization can follow expiry and dispatches no tools. This is a local POSIX/main-thread runner, not a generic cross-platform worker timeout.

resolved_findings.finding: Before dispatch, a public full visible prefix and pending call are appended, flushed and fsynced; after return, an updated journal is likewise written. Private journals are separate and do not enter causal views. A controlled interrupt records partial output and stops; a hard process kill leaves a pre-dispatch pending journal for read-only recovery. A pending call without a tool return becomes an explicitly harness-sourced unknown marker; existing observed tool returns are not duplicated or overwritten.
resolved_findings.limits: SIGKILL cannot write a final manifest or synthesized completion; preserve the surviving journal and do not rerun/resume the operation. No promise of perfect recovery from total disk failure or power loss is established by these file fsyncs. An interrupted journal append may have a truncated last record; recovery should use complete durable records and retain uncertainty.

additional_rechecks.finding: event_bundles accepts exactly the declared HARNESS_INTERRUPTED: effects unknown marker under harness_execution_record; the execution result is unknown. It never calls the original-return success decoder on that marker, and unknown harness strings are rejected.
